title: Slice Full-Resolution Joint-Evolution VLM Research Tree

nodes.title: Full-resolution Slice joint evolution
nodes.motivation: Train one native checkpoint for text, perception, generation, editing, reconstruction, segmentation, and world prediction without replacing the Slice field architecture.
nodes.action: Lock persistent X and H, ephemeral S, Slice/Deslice semantic writes, and capability-as-boundary-condition invariants.
nodes.conclusion: The product target is capability closure on one X-S-H graph; a particular energy-descent interpretation is supporting theory, not the target.
issues: Open-domain data and autoregressive text remain beyond the current synthetic closure.
nodes.invalidation: A matched causal experiment shows that a persistent full-resolution Slice write path cannot express the registered micro tasks while a topology-matched control can.

nodes.title: Slice read/deslice preserves thin structure
nodes.motivation: Test whether mass-normalized read and point-addressed write retain 1px structure.
nodes.action: Compared Slice and fair patch reconstruction heads on synthetic lines.
nodes.conclusion: Existing evidence supports Slice/Deslice as a useful full-resolution read/write mechanism.
issues: Evidence is synthetic and does not establish multimodal generation.
nodes.invalidation: A matched rerun removes the reported thin-structure advantage or identifies leakage.

nodes.title: NativeMoT X-S-H implementation
nodes.motivation: Make vision and language peer states connected by transient Slice communication.
nodes.action: Implemented full-resolution X, SliceRead, modality-private MoT experts, Deslice, and H evolution.
nodes.conclusion: The single-stack graph implements the core state topology; readout-controlled writes and RGB outer rollout were removed in the north-star closure.
issues: Multiple historical write/read knobs obscure the canonical path
nodes.invalidation: Code inspection or causal tests show that H or X bypasses the declared communication path.

nodes.title: Variational free-energy control
nodes.motivation: Use language priors and visual evidence to control inference and action.
nodes.action: Implemented Gaussian prior/posterior, KL surprise, accuracy, F, gap, and gates.
nodes.conclusion: Perception and generation share the F2 belief form. Generation also uses clean language priors and a causal Deslice(mu_p-S) prior-predictive action. Cross-layer common descent is neither established nor required for capability closure.
issues: Layer-specific coordinates make F values potentially incomparable
Surprise gating and F2 form are not themselves common-F descent
Current action omits learned precision weighting
nodes.invalidation: Analytical or empirical evidence shows the implemented F does not correspond to the claimed observation model.

nodes.title: Capabilities as boundary conditions and likelihoods
nodes.motivation: Use one graph for T2T, I2T, IT2T, reconstruction, I2I/T2I, segmentation, and next-frame prediction.
nodes.action: Added explicit image/text observation precision, target horizon, and terminal text/RGB/point-segmentation likelihoods to one Omni graph.
nodes.conclusion: Readout flags do not control X. Missing modalities and reconstruction-versus-future behavior are explicit boundary coordinates rather than black-image, empty-string, or port-ID shortcuts.
issues: Single-token class head remains only as checkpoint compatibility
Autoregressive Pythia token NLL is wired but not yet mixed into the capability matrix
The one-checkpoint fixed-bank audit is still running.
nodes.invalidation: A simpler, equivalent boundary-condition representation cannot reproduce the ports.

nodes.title: Current generation conflict
nodes.motivation: Test whether T2I emerges as active inference in the same graph.
nodes.action: Ran F-action, residual-read, S0, band, and real-apple probes; compared outer iteration counts.
nodes.conclusion: The invalid RGB loop was removed. The historical bundled VFE recipe fails, while both the simplified core and the minimal active-F2 recipe pass generation gates.
issues: Historical non-F2 mechanisms have not been reintroduced one at a time
Unseen continuous-coordinate generalization is untested
nodes.invalidation: A persistent-field implementation with fixed evaluation shows non-increasing common F and improving task metrics.

nodes.title: RGB round-trip breaks field persistence
nodes.motivation: Explain why additional generation iterations degrade output.
nodes.action: Compared K=1,2,4,8 on a fixed checkpoint and inspected f_generate.
nodes.conclusion: Quality degrades with K and each step rebuilds X from decoded RGB.
issues: Must compare against a true latent-field rollout.
nodes.invalidation: A controlled run shows RGB round-trip and latent rollout are equivalent in state and metrics.

nodes.title: Blank-field Slice addressing is weak
nodes.motivation: Explain color learning with weak digit geometry.
nodes.action: Held the graph fixed, simplified the objective/mechanisms, and trained 10 digits × 4 colors while retaining diffuse assignments.
nodes.conclusion: Generation reaches top1 1.00 with assignment entropy 0.978-0.996; diffuse assignment is not a capacity blocker.
issues: Assignment quality may still matter for position generalization, but did not explain the fixed-center failure.
nodes.invalidation: Fixed probes show stable prompt-dependent Slice geometry before successful generation.

nodes.title: Optimization and measurement favor false progress
nodes.motivation: Explain loss reduction and transient best-step spikes without robust generation.
nodes.action: Replaced the historical point-VFE bundle with balanced observation BCE, disabled bundled research knobs, and aligned the optimizer with the capacity gate.
nodes.conclusion: The same native Slice graph moves from chance to perfect digit identity; objective/mechanism bundling and optimization hid working capacity.
issues: Single-variable mechanism restoration and multi-seed confidence intervals are missing.
nodes.invalidation: Fixed-bank, per-time metrics reproduce stable gains across seeds.

nodes.title: North-star generation closure
nodes.motivation: Restore generation as a native Slice port instead of adding another generator.
nodes.action: Removed RGB outer rollout and readout-controlled writes, aligned training with a coordinate null source, and added a fixed-bank causal/assignment probe.
nodes.conclusion: Structural, prompt-causal, write-causal, fixed-center 10×4, named nine-grid, and active-F2 prior-action gates pass; continuous-coordinate generalization remains open. Common-F descent is an optional theory claim, not a generation gate.
issues: Unseen continuous position/jitter bank
Restore non-F2 research mechanisms one at a time
nodes.invalidation: The registered micro-capacity gate fails after structural and optimization checks while a topology-matched control passes.

nodes.title: Fixed-bank native generation audit
nodes.motivation: Test semantic causality and Slice addressing after restoring persistent-field generation.
nodes.action: Evaluated 40 deterministic center-digit cases with matched prompts, cyclically shuffled prompts, pi_x=0, and per-layer assignment diagnostics.
nodes.conclusion: The historical bundled VFE recipe remains at chance; this is recipe-specific, not a limitation of the Slice graph.
issues: The old flood metric also mislabeled black as colored flood
Bundled changes prevent single-mechanism attribution
nodes.invalidation: A registered rerun with the same topology produces >=0.50 matched-minus-shuffled top1 and passes the 0.95 capacity threshold across seeds.

nodes.title: Validated native digit generation core
nodes.motivation: Establish accurate generation before recurrence or active-inference claims.
nodes.action: Trained the non-shared four-layer Slice graph with balanced observation BCE and validated matched, digit-shuffled, and pi_x=0 controls.
nodes.conclusion: Fixed bank: matched top1 1.00, IoU 0.975, PSNR 44.71 dB; shuffled top1 0.00; pi_x=0 top1 0.10. The 10×4 capacity run also passes color and flood thresholds.
issues: Fixed center only
One training seed
VFE and recurrence deliberately absent
nodes.invalidation: A clean rerun fails the registered thresholds or reveals a prompt/Deslice bypass.

nodes.title: Flood metric correction
nodes.motivation: Prevent black ground from being counted as one-channel colored ink.
nodes.action: Added visible chroma and luminance requirements and a black-vs-green regression test.
nodes.conclusion: Perfect black ground now scores zero flood; historical flood values are versioned evidence, not directly comparable.
issues: Metric remains a synthetic-task diagnostic, not a natural-image quality measure.
nodes.invalidation: A palette edge case labels visibly black ground as flood or misses visibly colored ground.

nodes.title: Prompt-controlled nine-grid generation
nodes.motivation: Test whether language can control full-resolution write addresses without a position decoder or recurrent RGB loop.
nodes.action: Trained the same non-shared four-layer, 16-Slice core on digit × color × nine named positions and audited 90 fixed digit-position cases with digit-shuffled, position-shuffled, and pi_x=0 controls.
nodes.conclusion: Matched digit/color/paired IoU are 1.00. Digit shuffle drives top1 to 0; position shuffle preserves identity but drives paired IoU to 0; pi_x=0 removes identity, color, and position. Named spatial generation is prompt- and Slice-write-causal.
issues: Training-distribution positions, not unseen continuous coordinates
One training seed
VFE and recurrence deliberately absent
nodes.invalidation: A clean rerun fails the registered thresholds, or an ablation finds a non-Slice route from position words to pixels.

nodes.title: Active-F2 generation unification
nodes.motivation: Make accurate generation use the same variational belief form as F2 perception instead of remaining a baseline-only path.
nodes.action: Added a minimal active_f2 recipe on the validated core: Gaussian language prior/posterior, F2 gap training, clean-target prior in the t=0 chart, and Deslice(mu_p-S) prior-predictive action. Audited prompt, position, pi_x, and prior-action ablations on 90 fixed cases.
nodes.conclusion: Matched digit/color/position are 1.00 and F2 gaps are 0.00014-0.00073. Disabling only prior action drops top1 to 0.478; the active write is causal. active_f2 is now the canonical generation recipe and core is the control.
issues: Non-shared layer coordinates prevent a common-F descent claim
One seed
PSNR 62.93 is below the core control's 74.39
Prior action is isotropic rather than precision-weighted
nodes.invalidation: A registered rerun loses capacity or prior-action causality, or a bypass explains the ablation without the F2 write.

nodes.title: Fixed-coordinate common action-energy probe
nodes.motivation: Test whether the accurate non-shared generation trajectory reduces one comparable prior-predictive energy rather than arranging layer-private F values.
nodes.action: Recorded X0..X4 without changing the generator and scored every state with the frozen layer-0 SliceRead plus F2 language prior at fixed H0. Also compared the generated terminal field with Stem(clean target) and a re-encoded terminal RGB control.
nodes.conclusion: The common energy rises from 1.27620 to 1.32501 and no sample has lower terminal energy, while digit/color/location remain perfect. The existing implementation is not common-F descent. The anchor itself barely distinguishes clean target from blank, and the generated terminal field is in a different latent gauge from the perceptual Stem field.
issues: A blind anchor cannot support a useful monotonic regularizer
A common field chart or decoder-quotient energy is missing
The probe is one checkpoint and one seed
The result has not been independently reviewed
nodes.invalidation: A preregistered chart-closure model makes the shared preference distinguish clean target from blank, preserves generation capacity, and yields non-increasing common energy without a direct H-to-RGB write bypass.

nodes.title: North-star correction: capability closure before theory
nodes.motivation: Prevent the common-energy probe and recurrence theory from displacing the actual multimodal product objective.
nodes.action: Rewrote docs/NORTH_STAR.md around one-checkpoint capability closure and moved Hopfield/TTT/DeltaNet/common-F claims to supporting theory with separate evidence requirements.
nodes.conclusion: Per-layer attention may admit energy interpretations and global variational losses may be studied, but neither is a substitute for proving text, image, dense, and temporal capabilities on one native graph.
issues: The theory condition lattice still needs its own document and experiments.
nodes.invalidation: A required capability provably cannot be represented as a boundary/likelihood of the locked graph while a minimal topology change can.

nodes.title: Single-checkpoint capability closure
nodes.motivation: Replace separate port demonstrations with one checkpoint that jointly proves generation, perception, editing, reconstruction, segmentation, and world prediction.
nodes.action: Created four joint-supervision boundary cases on one colored-digit scene family, added fixed 360-sample auditing and modality/horizon interventions, and fine-tuned from the proven active-F2 generator.
nodes.conclusion: The first fixed-bank checkpoint scores 0.930 generation, 0.843 current perception/reconstruction, 0.865 editing, and 0.375 one-step future prediction. Text, image, and edit interventions are strongly causal; the horizon intervention fails, so capability closure is partial and the first checkpoint remains champion.
issues: Future address prediction is inaccurate
Text readout is categorical rather than autoregressive
Synthetic 16x16 task only
One seed
nodes.invalidation: Within the registered budget, one or more capability boundaries stay at chance or require a private computation path while a matched unified alternative succeeds.

nodes.title: LeJEPA and LeWM reference boundary
nodes.motivation: Separate the reusable world-model mechanism from JEPA anti-collapse regularization and avoid adding an unrelated generator.
nodes.action: Audited the official LeJEPA minimal implementation, LeWM paper, and LeWM predictor/rollout code. Documented the mapping in docs/LEJEPA_LEWM_REFERENCE.md and docs/NORTH_STAR.md.
nodes.conclusion: LeJEPA is architecture-agnostic view alignment plus SIGReg and has no AdaLN. LeWM uses a causal latent-history predictor and per-layer AdaLN-Zero action conditioning. Its next-latent MSE plus SIGReg is a fixed-variance, latent-only degeneration of the project's conditional VFE, not the full active-inference objective.
issues: The current digit bank has one frame and no explicit action
LeWM uses a global CLS latent whereas this project must retain full-resolution X
nodes.invalidation: Official source changes or code evidence show that LeJEPA itself contains the claimed temporal/action predictor or that LeWM does not use per-layer zero-initialized AdaLN.

nodes.title: Full-resolution dynamic-prior degeneration
nodes.motivation: Test whether LeWM-style temporal conditioning and next-state prediction close the failed future boundary without a separate world-model backbone.
nodes.action: Added live timestep embeddings into per-layer zero-AdaLN with exact tau=0 identity, then added a fixed-covariance KL between predicted future X and the observed-future X chart. Ran zero-AdaLN-only and zero-AdaLN-plus-transition-KL continuations from the first champion.
nodes.conclusion: Zero-AdaLN alone is insufficient (future 0.382, macro 0.696). Adding transition KL lowers its batch value from about 0.15 to 0.08 and improves future score to 0.415. Horizon-conditioned target position/segmentation IoU improves from 0.033/0.059 when ablated to 0.183/0.224 intact, but macro 0.736 remains below the 0.753 champion and absolute transport is poor.
issues: No causal history or action sequence in this historical run
Transition posterior uses only the sensory stem with fixed covariance
Generation and editing regress under future-heavy fine-tuning
The nine-grid list cycle is not a physical evolution benchmark
nodes.invalidation: Official or matched code evidence shows fixed Eulerian Slice read/write cannot predict nonlocal field evolution after history, action, dynamic covariance, and a valid temporal target are supplied.

nodes.title: Official Transolver temporal audit and address correction
nodes.motivation: Check whether Physics-Attention must move Slice addresses to evolve a Navier-Stokes field.
nodes.action: Audited the official Physics-Attention layer and NS benchmark. The layer reuses one slice assignment for read and deslice; the benchmark places ten historical values on every fixed grid point, predicts one next value, teacher-forces the rolling window in training, and autoregresses predictions in evaluation.
nodes.conclusion: Transolver performs field evolution on fixed Eulerian addresses. Nonlocal transport is represented by changes in field values through the learned operator, not by moving mesh addresses. The previous claim that shared read/write assignment is a necessary motion bottleneck is retracted.
issues: A shared low-rank basis may still limit capacity, but that is now an empirical ablation rather than an architectural necessity.
nodes.invalidation: The cited official code is shown to use distinct future query addresses or a hidden transport-deslice path for the reported NS experiment.

nodes.title: Causal-history active-inference transition closure
nodes.motivation: Close the concrete gaps identified by the Transolver, LeWM, V-JEPA2-AC, and JEPA-WMs audits without adding a private world-model backbone.
nodes.action: Added ordered full-resolution Eulerian history channels, explicit low-dimensional actions and action precision, action zero-AdaLN, per-target text/RGB/segmentation likelihood precision, and a same-graph diagonal-Gaussian KL between predictive prior and observed-future posterior. Replaced the arbitrary next-place list cycle with a periodic micro-world where history supplies inertial velocity and an independent action supplies an impulse.
nodes.conclusion: The interface and VFE topology are closed: pi=0 removes evidence exactly, history order is live, action gradients reach layer modulation, and q/p share the complete Slice-MoT-Deslice chart and uncertainty head. Seven focused tests and a one-step end-to-end training/audit smoke pass. Capability accuracy is not yet established, so the first checkpoint remains champion.
issues: A registered training run must show future accuracy and independent history/action causality without regressing generation, perception, or editing
Natural video and multi-step prior rollout remain untested
The synthetic action space is two-dimensional and periodic
nodes.invalidation: A matched trained run cannot use either history or action causally, the heteroscedastic KL collapses uncertainty, or the new interfaces degrade the already-passed capability gates.

nodes.title: SIGReg-active-inference correspondence audit
nodes.time: 2026-08-22 / arXiv 2607.13612 and official LeWM code audit
nodes.motivation: Determine whether SIGReg is already a variational-free-energy objective and whether it should be added to the explicit transition KL.
nodes.action: Audited the SIGReg-as-VFE theoretical preprint and the LeWM encoder, predictor, training objective, and configuration.
nodes.conclusion: Under fixed encoder noise and successful population isotropic-Gaussian enforcement, prediction plus SIGReg is an exact information-bottleneck/VFE degeneration. This is not an identity between finite-batch SIGReg and the project's per-sample state-conditional heteroscedastic KL. The explicit q-to-p KL remains primary and transition SIGReg stays off by default.
issues: The result is a 2026 theoretical preprint
Empirical validation is explicitly left for future work
Constant-noise and population Gaussian assumptions need independent checks
The derived objective lacks state-epistemic value
nodes.invalidation: A derivation or experiment shows the explicit state-conditional KL is absent or degenerate while SIGReg uniquely restores calibrated per-sample uncertainty without damaging spatial structure.

nodes.title: Private goal-action conditioning ablation
nodes.motivation: Test whether separating goal semantics from action dynamics removes condition interference and closes future prediction without SIGReg.
nodes.action: Split Goal and Action into private zero-AdaLN paths, froze conditioning biases so zero precision is exact identity, kept transition SIGReg at zero, and ran a 250-step continuation with a fixed 360-sample audit. Reverted the private paths after the failed causal audit.
nodes.conclusion: Full-bank generation/current/edit/future scores are 0.892/0.824/0.821/0.227 and the future primary score is 0.137. History ablation reduces the primary score by 0.022, but action, horizon, and future-goal ablations improve it by 0.030, 0.042, and 0.027. Separate channels preserve much of the static capability but do not create causal controlled dynamics; the checkpoint and mechanism are rejected and the previous champion remains active. Future admission requires intact action conditioning to beat action_precision=0 separately on paired-position IoU and segmentation IoU.
issues: Action remains a global affine modulation rather than a spatial token interaction
Only one seed and 250 continuation steps
Quick-gate edit accuracy also missed admission
Future transport remains poor
nodes.invalidation: A preregistered action-token-by-Slice causal operator with paired counterfactual supervision yields positive history, action, and horizon drops while preserving all three static capability gates.

nodes.title: Action-token by Slice causal operator
nodes.motivation: Test whether the failed action path lacked spatial interaction rather than merely a separate conditioning channel.
nodes.action: Replace uniform point-field and AdaLN action injection with one precision-masked action token in the native MoT sequence. Every layer's transient Slice can attend to the token; pi_a=0 masks it exactly, and text readout strips it. Keep one full-resolution X, the same Slice-MoT-Deslice path, the explicit heteroscedastic transition KL, and no SIGReg or recurrence.
nodes.conclusion: The full bank preserves static floors at 0.872/0.814/0.829 and history is weakly causal (+0.0188 primary). Action improves segmentation by 0.0078 but harms paired-position IoU by 0.0042, so it fails the preregistered two-metric gate. Horizon is strongly harmful (-0.0848 primary). The mechanism and checkpoint are rejected; the quick-bank admission was a sampling false positive.
issues: The predictive prior adds tau=1 into X while the observed-future posterior uses tau=0, violating the claimed common latent chart before KL
One pooled action token may still underrepresent multi-step action history
The action token uses the language expert rather than a third private QKV expert
One seed and a synthetic periodic micro-world
Not independently reviewed because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Either action metric is non-positive under ablation, static capability floors fail, or gains disappear under matched action shuffling/zero precision.

nodes.title: Control-token latent-chart closure
nodes.motivation: Remove the horizon coordinate mismatch exposed by the strongly negative tau ablation without changing the action-token hypothesis.
nodes.action: Keep target_time as an explicit boundary but encode nonzero tau as a precision-masked temporary MoT token. Do not add tau to persistent point field X, so predictive p and observed-future q end in the same latent coordinate chart before heteroscedastic KL. Keep action token, data, loss, budget, and all gates unchanged.
nodes.conclusion: Moving tau out of X reduces the harmful horizon primary drop from -0.0848 to -0.0175, supporting the chart-mismatch diagnosis, but does not make it causal. Action position becomes slightly positive (+0.0003) while segmentation becomes negative (-0.0055), and edit score regresses to 0.731. The checkpoint and horizon-token mainline configuration are rejected.
issues: A zero-content active control token still changes attention normalization
A horizon token changes the operator through MoT but does not prove calibrated continuous-time extrapolation
One seed
No independent review
nodes.invalidation: Horizon or either action dense metric remains non-positive on the full fixed bank, or p/q chart equality is broken by another direct control injection.

nodes.title: Action-relative Slice geometry
nodes.motivation: Test the remaining spatial-address hypothesis after global action tokens changed mask mass but failed to move the target position reliably.
nodes.action: Retain the action token and add a learned per-head bias to existing Slice-Slice attention. The bias sees destination-source Slice centroid displacement, the precision-weighted 2D action, and their residual. It is multiplied by action precision, uses current SliceRead assignments, adds no backbone or hand-coded shift, and leaves read/deslice addresses fixed. Revert the failed horizon-token configuration for this isolated action test.
nodes.conclusion: The full bank passes static floors at 0.885/0.837/0.823. Action paired-position and segmentation drops are both positive for the first time (+0.00029/+0.00213), and history is positive on both (+0.0141/+0.0237). This passes the preregistered sign test but the effect is too small for a capability claim; the quick edit gate missed and horizon remains strongly harmful (-0.1008). The checkpoint is not promoted.
issues: Action effect size is near zero and untested across seeds
Slice centroids are soft and may be poorly localized
The learned relation sees raw toy translation coordinates and needs later generalization
Horizon remains a separate unresolved control problem
One seed and no independent review
nodes.invalidation: Either action dense metric is non-positive, static floors fail, or action gradients do not reach the relation bias under pi_a=1 while pi_a=0 remains exact identity.

nodes.title: Deconfounded transition-boundary gate
nodes.motivation: Remove the perfect training-set confound tau=1 iff action is observed, which prevents independent identification of transition horizon and action content.
nodes.action: Make tau gate whether an observed action is executed by the transition operator, without injecting tau into persistent X. Add tau=0 current-state samples containing a proposed nonzero action and tau=1 future samples containing an observed no-op. Retain action token, relative Slice bias, losses, budget, and static gates.
nodes.conclusion: All registered causal dense signs become positive: horizon/action paired-position and segmentation are +0.00142/+0.00030, and history is +0.00708/+0.01958. However current and edit scores fall to 0.745/0.749, below the static floors, and absolute future primary falls to 0.113. The causal boundary is identifiable but shared future training overwrites proven capabilities; the checkpoint is rejected.
issues: Horizon gates action execution by construction, so horizon and action effects remain mechanistically related
No-op actions dilute the average action ablation
Shared trunk optimization causes severe static regression
One seed and no independent review
nodes.invalidation: Any causal dense metric is non-positive, static floors fail, or improvements arise only because tau directly selects an output/readout path.

nodes.title: Static-capability-preserving transition stage
nodes.motivation: Test whether v9 failed from gradient interference after establishing that all transition controls have the correct causal sign.
nodes.action: Initialize from the static champion, gate both history and action by nonzero horizon, and train only history/action encoders, action token, action-relative Slice bias, and transition log-variance. Freeze the proven Slice-MoT-Deslice trunk, RGB/text/segmentation readouts, and all static interfaces. Keep the v9 counterfactual bank and budget.
nodes.conclusion: Horizon/history/action dense signs are all positive and future primary rises to 0.139; generation/edit remain 0.930/0.865. Current falls to 0.497 before any trainable-parameter effect: parameter and forward diffs show the cause is the false auxiliary assumption that history should be gated off at tau=0. History is current-state evidence, not a transition control. The checkpoint and history gate are rejected.
issues: The preregistered history-gating assumption was conceptually wrong
Freezing may prevent the representation from learning a transport basis
The transition log-variance head remains trainable but RGB/seg heads are fixed
One seed and no independent review
nodes.invalidation: Static floors regress despite exact control gating, any causal sign reverses, or temporal-only parameters receive no gradient.

nodes.title: Action-only protected transition stage
nodes.motivation: Correct the history-as-control category error while retaining v10's evidence that protected optimization improves transition causality.
nodes.action: Keep ordered history visible and freeze its champion stem. Gate only action execution by horizon. Train only action encoders/token, action-relative Slice bias, and transition log-variance; freeze the shared trunk, history stem, and all static readouts. Keep the counterfactual bank and 250-step budget.
nodes.conclusion: Generation/edit and several transition signs survive, but current remains 0.520 and action/history segmentation signs turn slightly negative. Parameter and forward audits show the static champion never trained history_stem; removing target_time_coord changed random initialization, and the protected stage then froze a random history encoder. This run is invalid as a test of protected action adaptation and its checkpoint is rejected.
issues: Initialization did not include a trained history stem
Frozen random history representation invalidates the intended comparison
One seed and no independent review
nodes.invalidation: Any static floor or dense causal sign fails, or future primary falls below 0.113.

nodes.title: History-closed protected action stage
nodes.motivation: Run the intended protected action test from a checkpoint that actually contains the trained history basis.
nodes.action: Initialize the horizon-gated counterfactual model from v8, which has static scores 0.885/0.837/0.823 and trained history/action-relative modules. Drop only the harmful target_time_coord, then train action modules and transition log-variance for 250 steps with all history/static/shared parameters frozen.
nodes.conclusion: Static floors are preserved at 0.885/0.837/0.823 and future score rises from the audited 0.435 initialization to 0.485. However horizon and action paired-position/segmentation drops are both negative, and history position is negative. Protected action training optimizes easy future attributes while erasing controlled spatial causality; the checkpoint is rejected.
issues: The aggregate future loss does not protect action-relative transport
v8 itself came from one seed
The pre-training future score uses the new counterfactual bank and is not comparable to v8's published old-bank score
No independent review
nodes.invalidation: Any static floor or causal dense sign fails after training, or the trained checkpoint does not improve a registered future quantity over its audited initialization.

nodes.title: Static-future gradient conflict projection
nodes.motivation: Prevent aggregate future optimization from improving easy attributes by overwriting static capability or action-relative transport.
nodes.action: Use separate static and future minibatches. On shared trainable parameters, project away only the component of the future gradient that has negative inner product with the static gradient; future-only action parameters retain their full gradient. Keep model, counterfactual bank, VFE terms, v8 initialization, total examples per step, and 250-step budget fixed.
nodes.conclusion: Static floors pass at 0.871/0.788/0.913 and history position/segmentation drops are positive (+0.0116/+0.0101). Action and horizon position/segmentation drops are both negative (-0.00073/-0.00081), and future score 0.321 is below the audited 0.435 initialization. The final recorded static-future gradient inner product is positive and projection coefficient zero, so global PCGrad does not target the missing counterfactual action relation. The checkpoint is rejected.
issues: Global task-gradient alignment can be positive while action-specific spatial gradients are wrong
Projection activation was recorded only at evaluation, not every step
PCGrad protects static gradients but not explicitly action causality
Two forward graphs per step add overhead
One seed and no independent review
nodes.invalidation: Static floors or any dense causal sign fails, future score falls below initialization, or recorded gradient projection is never active.

nodes.title: Counterfactual action objective is the next missing object
nodes.motivation: Stop adding generic conditioning and optimization mechanisms after repeated action-causality failures.
nodes.action: Compared private/global AdaLN, action tokens, horizon tokens, action-relative Slice attention, deconfounded boundaries, protected staging, and global gradient projection under fixed causal audits.
nodes.conclusion: Action-relative Slice geometry can make both dense action signs weakly positive on the old bank, and counterfactual data can make all transition controls positive when the shared trunk adapts, but aggregate VFE/observation losses do not preserve that relation together with static capability. The next admissible experiment must directly contrast predictions under paired actions for the same state/history, or train a controlled Slice write-transport likelihood. It must not add SIGReg, another backbone, recurrence, or a task-private output path.
issues: Direct action contrast must be formulated inside the explicit VFE rather than as an unrelated auxiliary classifier
A dynamic write operator must preserve fixed full-resolution X and the Slice semantic write route
Effect sizes need multiple seeds
No independent review
nodes.invalidation: A simpler registered loss rebalance, without counterfactual action contrast or controlled write transport, produces robust positive action/horizon/history dense effects and all static floors across seeds.

nodes.title: Paired counterfactual action likelihood
nodes.motivation: Make action identity affect the observation likelihood directly instead of hoping that an aggregate future loss preserves the action-to-transport relation.
nodes.action: For each future state/history, form the five matched interventions left, right, up, down, and no-op. Run the same Slice-MoT model once per intervention and construct a pairwise RGB plus segmentation negative-log-likelihood energy matrix between every prediction and every counterfactual target. Add a symmetric contrast over negative energy so the matched action-target diagonal must have the lowest free energy. Use two five-action groups plus fourteen static samples per step, PCGrad only as the already-defined static rehearsal guard, v8 initialization, one fixed 250-step run, coefficient 1.0, temperature 0.1, and no new backbone, head, recurrence, SIGReg, or action classifier.
nodes.conclusion: The registered prediction failed. The final training batch has a positive but tiny diagonal energy gap (+0.000373), while the symmetric contrast remains 1.616, near random five-way log(5). The selected step-200 checkpoint passes generation/current floors at 0.858/0.761 but narrowly misses edit at 0.798; future primary is 0.109, below the v8 initialization 0.435. History position/segmentation are both positive (+0.0122/+0.0106), but action and horizon share negative position/segmentation effects (-0.00113/-0.00758). The checkpoint is rejected. Direct paired observation contrast is not sufficient when the action path cannot reliably control the Deslice destination; the next structural test is a learned action-conditioned Slice write-transport likelihood on the same X-S-H graph.
issues: Single seed and 250 steps
RGB MSE plus categorical segmentation NLL is a registered finite observation model, not a proof of globally descending free energy
PCGrad never projected at the final recorded step because the global gradient dot product was positive
The selected rejected checkpoint is step 200 while the reported final-batch energy gap is from step 250
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Any static floor fails; action paired-position or segmentation gain is not greater than 0.005; history or horizon has a non-positive dense gain; matched diagonal energy is not below off-diagonal energy; future score is below 0.435; or future primary does not exceed 0.109.

nodes.title: Action-grid coordinate chart repair
nodes.motivation: The world actions are encoded as (dx,dy), while coords() and Slice centroids are ordered (y,x); the relative-action feature currently subtracts these incompatible charts directly.
nodes.action: Convert the geometric action to (dy,dx) only at the Slice-relative geometry boundary, add a regression test that inspects the relation feature, and rerun the exact v14 paired-likelihood protocol from v8 for 250 steps. Keep data, sample budget, losses, learning rates, PCGrad guard, action token, model parameter count, checkpoint floors, and 0.005 causal effect gate unchanged.
nodes.conclusion: The coordinate feature is now correct and its regression test passes, but the registered capability prediction failed. The selected step-250 checkpoint has generation/current/edit 0.855/0.726/0.833, so current misses its floor. Future primary is 0.106. History position/segmentation remain positive (+0.0108/+0.00919), while action position is negative and segmentation is sub-threshold (-0.000274/+0.00114). The diagonal energy gap is only +0.000254 and contrast is 1.617. The axis mismatch was a real implementation error but not the dominant causal bottleneck; learned action-conditioned Slice write transport is now justified.
issues: The existing MLP could learn an axis permutation, consistent with the small change
PCGrad activated at the final step but did not restore the missing action relation
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Any v14 gate fails or the coordinate feature presented to the relation MLP is not exactly (dy,dx).

nodes.title: Learned Slice write-transport likelihood
nodes.motivation: v14-v15 show that action information and paired observation energy are present, but Deslice still writes through the same assignment used to read the current field.
nodes.action: Add one zero-initialized learned 2x2 action-to-displacement map per existing Slice layer. It transports only the Slice assignment field by differentiable periodic semi-Lagrangian sampling on fixed Eulerian addresses; semantic values still evolve through the same MoT and write through the same Deslice. Blend is exactly zero for missing action, no-op, or tau=0. Keep the v15 action token, relative bias, paired VFE, PCGrad guard, v8 initialization, two five-action groups plus fourteen static samples, 250 steps, and all thresholds unchanged.
nodes.conclusion: The registered prediction failed. Exact zero/no-op/tau=0 identity and transport gradients pass, and all four learned 2x2 maps become nonzero, but their per-layer displacements stay below 0.1 pixel and partly cancel. The selected step-200 checkpoint has static scores 0.838/0.825/0.832, so generation misses its floor; future primary is 0.114 and future score 0.344. History position/segmentation remain positive (+0.0129/+0.0124), while action is harmful (-0.00760/-0.00458). The final-batch energy gap is only +0.000125. A read-only audit finds per-layer assignment spatial standard deviation only 0.0069-0.0118 and Deslice write spatial standard deviation 0.00036-0.00129, so transporting a near-uniform assignment cannot express a one-cell move. The minimal assignment-transport form is rejected and remains off by default. The next theoretical object, if pursued, must evolve spatially resolved persistent belief content rather than merely advect diffuse assignment probabilities.
issues: Periodic advection is a disclosed micro-world inductive bias and must not be presented as learned general physics
A global 2D displacement per layer cannot represent deformation or object-specific actions
Applying the same action at four layers permits cancellation and confounds depth with physical time
The persistent X mixes content and fixed coordinate embeddings, so blindly advecting X would corrupt its coordinate chart
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Any registered gate fails, zero-action identity breaks, transport gradients vanish, or the observed gain can be reproduced with the transport map held at zero.

nodes.title: Unified F2 action as a Slice transition prior
nodes.motivation: Generation already succeeds through the F2 prior action Deslice(mu_p-S), whereas physical action only perturbs attention before the same-address write. The missing object may be an explicit action-conditioned transition of the Slice belief itself.
nodes.action: In the first physical transition only, construct a column-normalized T_a(destination Slice | source Slice, belief) from destination-source soft centroid displacement, the correctly charted action, and their residual. Apply S_write <- T_a S_write immediately after the existing language/F2 prior is formed, then use the unchanged fixed-address Deslice(w_read). Blend with identity by executed action magnitude so missing action, no-op, and tau=0 are exact identity. Keep one X-S-H graph, all existing likelihoods, the paired counterfactual VFE, PCGrad static guard, v8 initialization, 14 static plus 10 paired-future examples, and 250 steps. Disable the failed assignment transport.
nodes.conclusion: The registered prediction failed. Generation/edit pass at 0.875/0.835, current misses at 0.733, future primary is 0.116, and action position/segmentation are both negative (-0.000593/-0.000345) while history is strongly positive (+0.0103/+0.0200). Holding only T_a at identity leaves both dense metrics exactly unchanged. Parameters receive gradients, but the fixed +8 identity logit keeps the learned executed-action matrix at mean diagonal 0.99499, maximum off-diagonal 0.000334, and mean absolute identity deviation 0.000626. Therefore v17 did not instantiate a usable transition range; it rejects the saturated identity parameterization, not the Slice-transition hypothesis or VFE action.
issues: Soft Slice centroids remain weakly localized
The +8 identity logit created an optimization saturation not included in the core theory
The micro-world has global translations only
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Any registered metric gate fails; T_a is applied more than once; column normalization or exact identity boundaries fail; transition parameters receive no gradient; or holding T_a at identity preserves the claimed action gain.

nodes.title: Non-saturated stochastic Slice action
nodes.motivation: v17's transition was mathematically normalized but practically locked to identity by a +8 diagonal logit, so its zero-transition ablation could not distinguish the mechanism.
nodes.action: Replace the saturated softmax parameterization with T_a=(1-rho_a)I+rho_a P_a, where P_a is column-softmax of the same centroid/action score and rho_a=||a|| sigmoid(r) is a learned execution rate initialized to 0.1. Missing action, no-op, and tau=0 remain exact identity; active actions start in a non-saturated range. Change no data, backbone, likelihood, paired VFE coefficient, optimizer, budget, initialization, or gates from v17.
nodes.conclusion: The non-saturated transition changes the result pattern but does not pass. Static generation/current/edit all pass at 0.891/0.764/0.901 and history position/segmentation are positive (+0.0116/+0.0184). Overall action becomes weakly double-positive (+0.00185/+0.00170) on the full counterfactual bank, but remains below the registered 0.005 effect floor. The learned rate is 0.10046 and T_a clearly departs from identity (mean diagonal 0.9058, maximum off-diagonal 0.00628), yet holding only T_a at identity leaves paired IoU exactly unchanged and improves segmentation by 0.000214. Thus the old action token/attention path, not T_a, explains the weak gain. This rules out saturation as the sole cause and shifts the conflict to the use of diffuse soft centroids/Slice slots as stable dynamical addresses and to the absence of a posterior-aligned transition likelihood. The checkpoint is rejected and the mechanism remains experimental/off by default.
issues: The 0.1 initial rate is an explicit optimization assumption
The learned proposal remains near diffuse mixing
Soft Slice slots are transient and not guaranteed to keep identity between current prior and future posterior
The paired RGB/segmentation likelihood does not directly identify which future Slice corresponds to which source Slice
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Any v17 gate fails, transition stays effectively identity, or transition ablation is non-causal.

nodes.title: Active-inference GDN-2 causal Slice belief
nodes.motivation: v18 moves a transient Slice transition but its identity ablation is null, implying that an action has no persistent, posterior-aligned state address on which to act.
nodes.action: Introduce one shared fixed spatial atlas and a persistent factorized Gaussian fast-weight belief represented by natural parameters and precision. Ordered physical history updates the belief through the shared first-layer SliceRead. Dynamic process variance releases obsolete precision; observation likelihood precision writes natural parameters; inferred velocity and explicit action shift causal source queries. The returned prior writes only through the existing first Deslice residual. Add a same-chart future Slice KL, external causal-state I/O, exact zero-precision/zero-horizon boundaries, a causal-memory ablation, mechanism tests, and an opt-in training flag. Do not use network depth as time or add another generator/backbone.
nodes.conclusion: Implementation and mechanism evidence only: the full local suite passes after adding focused tests. A one-step from-scratch smoke has finite full-field transition KL 0.0298 and causal Slice KL 0.6362, but exposed that the first landing used a 0.5 sigmoid gain and therefore was not champion-preserving. The landing was corrected to an exactly zero-initialized residual projection with a live first-step gradient; the old smoke is retained only as numerical evidence and is invalid as a performance comparison. No capability claim is made and the feature remains disabled by default pending a registered continuation.
issues: Stable atlas identity is an architectural assumption and content-address correction may still drift
The current factorized Gaussian address belief is not exact full-covariance Bayesian linear regression
Motion correspondence is learned from Slice content and may fail under occlusion or deformation
The periodic nine-grid action scale is a disclosed initialization, not learned general physics
A registered continuation from the proven generator and multiple seeds have not run
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Reject or revise if a registered continuation fails any static floor; history, action, horizon, or causal-memory ablation is non-positive on either paired IoU or segmentation IoU; the same-index atlas is worse than permutation-matched posterior alignment; zero-precision or zero-horizon identity breaks; or gains vanish when parameter count and training budget are matched.

nodes.title: Persistent atlas landing versus transient Deslice
nodes.motivation: The Gaussian state has stable addresses, but its first implementation landed through the current content-dependent Slice assignment and could discard that identity.
nodes.action: Compare equal-budget 50-step temporal continuations from v18. v19 queries persistent memory but lands through transient w_read; v20 uses fixed point-to-atlas weights through the same additive X residual. Preserve zero-initialized behavior, static floors, data, optimizer, likelihoods, and causal audits.
nodes.conclusion: v19 initially looked positive but a continuation made causal-memory segmentation harmful. v20 at 50 steps preserves generation/current/edit 0.910/0.764/0.901, gives action +0.00473/+0.00406 and causal-memory +0.00292/+0.00280, and is clearly better under the same budget. A 100-step continuation overtrains and makes memory position slightly negative, so v20-50 is retained as evidence but not a robust champion.
issues: One seed
Effects remain below 0.005
Longer training regresses
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Reject fixed atlas landing if a matched transient landing produces larger positive causal-memory effects on both dense metrics without static regression.

nodes.title: Predict-before-correct history transport
nodes.motivation: A Bayesian filter normally predicts the previous state into the current chart before assimilating the next observation; v20 only inferred velocity and used it at the terminal query.
nodes.action: Transport Gaussian mean and variance between consecutive history observations before correction, repair duplicate periodic atlas endpoints, and rerun the matched 50-step continuation.
nodes.conclusion: The theoretically fuller filter regresses relative to v20: action falls to +0.00380/+0.00321 and causal-memory to +0.00129/+0.00090. Inferred correspondence is not reliable enough to move stored belief. History transport is therefore an explicit flag that defaults off; a formal predict step is not admitted merely because it is theoretically attractive.
issues: Velocity confidence is not calibrated
Content correspondence may mix background and digit
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Reopen only when a precision-gated or externally identified correspondence improves both causal-memory metrics over v20 under a matched budget.

nodes.title: Future language boundary deconfounding
nodes.motivation: Every audit showed that removing the literal Predict next frame prompt improved future dense metrics, suggesting a task label was being treated as semantic evidence.
nodes.action: Set prompt and text precision to missing only for world samples with no semantic instruction; retain history, horizon, action, output text likelihood, and all static language boundaries. Add a CLI flag so historical comparisons remain reproducible. Then isolate full-memory, projection-only, and sole-action-path variants.
nodes.conclusion: Without the vacuous prompt, future primary rises from about 0.117 to 0.153, history primary effect rises to about +0.025, and action position effect becomes large and positive. Whole-memory, arbitrary projection-only, and GDN-only action continuations still fail their causal-memory ablations, showing that boundary deconfounding is necessary but does not close the latent coordinate chart.
issues: The microbenchmark prompt contains no target semantics
Natural-language future instructions must be retested separately
One seed
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Restore the label as evidence if it contains target semantics or if a matched run improves future primary and all causal signs without it being ablated.

nodes.title: Closed content-coordinate dynamic prior
nodes.motivation: A mechanism probe found the transient-atlas prior delta almost orthogonal to the true full-resolution change. The persistent X mixed movable RGB content with immobile xy coordinates, and dense learned landing maps could relearn incompatible charts.
nodes.action: Define X_content as encode(image) minus encode(black at the same coordinates and precision). Fixed-atlas Slice, Gaussian update, action/velocity query, and fixed Deslice scatter all operate in that X-content chart. Keep semantic F2 generation separate and gate physical write by tau only. Replace the dense prior projection with a per-channel trust gate; keep library trust zero for exact checkpoint identity and use the audited 0.1 warm start for the physical experiment.
nodes.conclusion: v29 is the first active-memory checkpoint with both causal-memory dense signs positive while preserving all static floors. Generation/current/edit are 0.891/0.764/0.901; future primary is 0.15415. Causal-memory position/segmentation gains are +0.00040/+0.00073, history +0.02172/+0.03085, and total action +0.01941/+0.00134. This resolves the sign conflict but not the robustness gate: action segmentation and memory effects remain below 0.005, and future accuracy is still weak. The result is partial, not a completed world model.
issues: Single seed
Audited trust 0.1 is an optimization prior
The fixed factorized atlas is low rank
Action segmentation gain is below 0.005
No independent review because delegation is disabled
nodes.invalidation: Reject as a mainline world model if multiple seeds lose either causal-memory sign, any static floor regresses, action segmentation remains below 0.005 after a registered scale test, or gains disappear with a matched parameter/budget control.

nodes.title: Frozen Pythia as token observation model
nodes.motivation: Replace the single-class text readout with a pretrained causal token likelihood on the same Slice–MoT graph, without a second VLM or an image generator.
nodes.action: Wired exact Pythia-70m load and forward_tokens. Bound frozen embeddings to the generation champion by training language-side MoT readers plus digit-shuffle. Fixed labels=None NLL leak, added eval-only, zero-init text_out/proj residual gates, and a token_interface phase. Named-edit source-shuffle was implemented then disabled at the train call site; modal precision was allocated but not passed; language_rgb unfroze pix_head. Retraining uses edit_spatial, explicit pi_x=0/1, and a live edit-shuffle coefficient. Documented in docs/STATUS.md.
nodes.conclusion: Phase A is in. Pythia T2I on the 90-cell mixed-color grid passes (digit 0.967, color 0.988, IoU 0.960, shuffles ~0) at checkpoints/omni_d64_pythia_language_best.pt. Official capability edit is next-color, not named-color. A 400-step named-color run is not a frozen-read invalidation: source-shuffle was off during optimization, pix_head was free, and flood 0.59 is a global-color shortcut. Token NLL and graph decode remain open.
issues: IT2I next-color edit is unsolved under Pythia
Named-color edit_spatial: no geometry gap; flood low with pix_head frozen
Named-color edit_read (unfreeze SliceRead/Wq_v/Wo_v/Deslice at 1e-5): still no geometry gap; T2I never holds 0.95; flood rises to 0.20 once Deslice moves; no ckpt saved
Pythia-70m is not instruction-tuned; graph decode is not implemented
No mixed-port token-NLL training yet
nodes.invalidation: Token NLL bypasses MoT, answer tokens write X, or requesting Pythia silently loads GPT-2/TinyLM.

nodes.title: Unified static Pythia capability closure
nodes.motivation: The generation-only Pythia checkpoint could not reconstruct its input, and named-color editing remained source-invariant. Audit showed that the initialization lacked current-frame capability, reconstruction leaked a pi_text=1 task label, and the old T2I and capability banks used different stroke generators.
nodes.action: Start from northstar_slice_capability_best.pt; use capability_sample/grid_digit_mask for T2I, current reconstruction/segmentation, and official next-color editing; set reconstruction text evidence to missing at tau=0; initialize the existing Pythia text_in by ridge alignment to the toy champion's post-text_in lexical chart; train same-color/same-address ten-digit groups with a 10x10 RGB+segmentation observation-energy likelihood; keep Pythia, stem, SliceRead, Deslice, and segmentation head frozen; open the shared RGB head only during low-rate generation warmup; admit editing only after T2I and current gates pass.
nodes.conclusion: Independent reload of checkpoints/omni_d64_pythia_capability_b3_edit_best.pt passes all registered static visual gates. T2I digit/color/paired-IoU are 1.000/0.963/0.936 with digit and color shuffles at 0. Current reconstruction digit/color/paired-IoU/seg-IoU are 0.911/0.903/0.883/0.975 with source-IoU gap 0.827. Official next-color edit digit/color/paired-IoU/seg-IoU are 0.878/0.940/0.697/0.991 with source digit/IoU gaps 0.789/0.631 and flood 0.028. This resolves the source-geometry failure without unfreezing the visual read/write path.
issues: Autoregressive token NLL and graph decode remain untrained
IT2T next-color text output is not yet closed
The ridge anchors use the synthetic capability vocabulary and must be replaced or expanded for natural language
The result is one synthetic scene family and one seed
The old generation-only checkpoint remains a separate historical proof, not the unified checkpoint
nodes.invalidation: Any independent reload fails a registered T2I/current/edit gate; source shuffling does not reduce edit geometry; the result depends on a second scene generator or a bypass head; Pythia becomes trainable; or token training later destroys any static gate.

nodes.title: Causal token likelihood and graph-native decode
nodes.motivation: The B3 checkpoint closed static visual likelihoods but still had no autoregressive text observation or decode path, so it could not demonstrate T2T, I2T, or IT2T with the frozen causal language distribution.
nodes.action: Add a unified token collator with per-token precision, a legal zero-precision BOS for missing text, an explicit visual_prompt_mask that excludes teacher-forced and generated answer tokens, matched/shuffled token-NLL gates, identified answer-set NLL on the same Pythia logits, a read-only token_reader phase, and greedy decode that reruns forward_tokens for every token. Then repair the training protocol instead of the architecture: pure-I2T long run with hard-cell replay, I2T-heavy rehearsal cycle, Adam-state resume, and low-rate high-contrast finishing.
nodes.conclusion: The first unified token champion is admitted. checkpoints/omni_d64_pythia_token_best.pt independently reloads with T2T token/greedy 1.000/1.000, I2T 0.822/0.811 (full 90-cell bank, median matched-vs-shuffled gap 7.47 nat), official next-color IT2T 1.000/1.000, and all three protected static gates intact. The earlier 0.444 candidate was protocol-limited, not capacity-limited: a 2000-step pure-I2T run lifts the isolated ceiling to 0.667, and joint rehearsal from that state with hard replay no longer erodes I2T (0.667 to 0.778 while T2T/IT2T return to 1.000). Shrunk paths: starting the visual residual gate at embedding magnitude is worse (0.556), refuting the amplitude hypothesis; opening penultimate-layer H-only experts is rejected because their H output feeds the next block's Kt and moves X (test-pinned).
issues: The token audit bank is a registered subset of the training bank; this is finite-bank closure, not held-out generalization
I2T leaves 16 of 90 cells wrong with diffuse digit and place spread
Single seed for every run in the admission chain
Pythia-70m is a base model; the missing-text BOS interface is not pretrained
The fixed 4x4 terminal atlas and prototype/ridge initialization remain default-off
nodes.invalidation: Reject the token champion if an independent reload fails any token, decode, or static gate; if answer or generated tokens can change X or earlier logits; if lm.generate is called; if Pythia becomes trainable; or if a held-out bank without training-bank overlap cannot close the I2T accuracy gate.

nodes.title: Real ShareGPT-4o port pilot and boundary correction
nodes.motivation: Move beyond the colored-digit micro-world and test whether real T2I, IT2I, and image-conditioned text records can enter the locked X-Slice-H graph without a diffusion generator, private visual backbone, or language bypass; audit rather than assume each dataset's task boundary.
nodes.action: Normalize FreedomIntelligence ShareGPT-4o-Image generation/edit pairs and gated OpenGVLab ShareGPT-4o conversations as boundary conditions and terminal likelihoods. Add aspect-preserving fields, resumable partial-tar and remote-ZIP64 sampling, answer-to-vision masks, heteroscedastic natural-RGB likelihood, FP32 categorical likelihood over frozen-FP16 Pythia logits, matched/shuffled controls, deterministic per-port holdouts, and candidate-only narrow phases. Scan all 57,289 first-turn one-image OpenGV rows, correct caption paraphrase classification, materialize 134 T2I, 142 IT2I, and 512 I2T records, and train the I2T terminal reader at 64x64.
nodes.conclusion: All 930 referenced images verify. The OpenGV scan found only generic caption requests and zero genuine question/instruction-conditioned IT2T; the earlier 128-IT2T claim and its metrics are invalidated. The clean RGB-likelihood run still improves T2I/IT2I/reconstruction while retaining every B3 gate. For corrected held-out I2T, NLL falls from 9.977 to 4.602 but only 52.9% of samples have positive shuffle gaps. A stricter real-image curriculum exposed missing EOS supervision and then passed finite-sample capacity gates: frozen Pythia plus token_reader reaches graph-greedy/rotated exact 5/5, 16/16, and 32/32; the 32-image gate has NLL 0.0339, token accuracy 99.7%, and EOS 32/32. Rotating images rotates every answer, and reloaded static T2I/current/edit gates all pass. Thus finite-sample expressivity and the training interface are established, while held-out open-domain I2T remains unadmitted.
issues: The two specified datasets contain no genuine IT2T/VQA supervision
I2T positive causal-gap fraction is only 52.9% and the mean gap shrinks during fitting
T2I prompt causality remains effectively zero
No qualitative natural-image geometry or graph-decode gate
No multiple seeds
nodes.invalidation: Reject real-data readiness if captions are mislabeled as IT2T, if held-out likelihood improves without a robust positive matched-vs-shuffled gap, if protected static gates regress, or if success requires an output-private backbone, trainable Pythia, answer leakage, or lm.generate.

nodes.title: Joint fixed-bank 1px OCR and native generation
nodes.motivation: Test the minimal claim requested by the project owner: the same checkpoint should be able to memorize original noisy 1px OCR while retaining native 1px text-to-image generation; held-out generalization is not required for this gate.
nodes.action: Append one deterministic hard noisy Bresenham 1px image per digit to the passed 32-real-image I2T curriculum. Keep Pythia and all visual read/write paths frozen, train only token_reader with 3:1 real-I2T/OCR rehearsal, supervise EOS, save graph-greedy-selected model and Adam state, and use low-rate paired replay for competing visual addresses. Independently reload the final checkpoint and audit the protected static T2I/current/edit banks.
nodes.conclusion: The final single checkpoint reaches real-I2T 32/32 and noisy 1px OCR 10/10 graph-greedy exact; rotated images are 42/42 and all answers terminate. Independent reload preserves native 1px digit T2I generation on 117 prompts with digit/color/paired-IoU 1.000/0.969/0.941, digit and color shuffle scores 0, and flood 0.00165. Current reconstruction/segmentation and next-color edit also pass. Therefore finite-bank OCR and generation coexistence is established under frozen Pythia and one X-Slice-H graph.
issues: OCR uses one fixed noisy 1px image per digit
Generation is the fixed synthetic digit/color/address bank, not natural-image generation
Targets are closed-set or compact and do not establish open-domain generalization
No multiple seeds
nodes.invalidation: Reject the coexistence claim if any fixed OCR digit fails graph-greedy decode, image rotation does not rotate answers, the 1px T2I gate regresses, Pythia or a private OCR head becomes trainable, lm.generate is called, or the checkpoint cannot be independently reloaded.

nodes.title: Natural-image native T2I finite-bank capacity
nodes.motivation: Test whether the same native full-resolution Slice graph can freely write dense natural RGB from text and an explicitly missing visual observation, rather than only generate sparse synthetic digits.
nodes.action: Select two visually distinct Freedom ShareGPT-4o T2I targets; feed an all-zero field with image precision zero; keep Pythia frozen and skip its causal decoder; train only language-to-visual messages, F2 prior, Slice/Deslice visual query-output, modality precision, and the shared RGB Gaussian likelihood. Require 2/2 prompt retrieval, PSNR at least 20 dB, and a positive rotated-prompt MSE gap. Independently audit the protected T2I/current/edit banks; also test terminal RGB/seg teacher replay as a retention control.
nodes.conclusion: The original pixel-only decision was a false positive. At 16x16, prompt retrieval is 2/2 and PSNR 20.16 dB with a +0.185 prompt-shuffle gap, but direct display of the original ShareGPT PNG shows only coarse color/layout; edge relative MSE/correlation are 0.803/0.426 and fail the registered 0.75/0.50 content gate. At 64x64 with 16 slices, PSNR is 19.04 and edge correlation 0.133. Opening the existing visual stem/KV/FFN/local path, expanding to 64 slices, setting Gaussian NLL weight to zero, and strongly supervising edges yields a coarse mask outline but only PSNR 15.64 and edge correlation 0.190 after 600 steps; island and boat structure remain absent. Natural content capacity is not established. The model can select prompt-specific low-frequency fields, and no source image, private generator, lm.generate, or trainable Pythia is used.
issues: Only two fixed targets and one seed
Pixel PSNR is dominated by low-frequency color and cannot serve as the natural-image gate
Current transient Slice/Deslice writes lack sufficient learned high-frequency address structure
Increasing slices and opening existing visual content layers is insufficient
All natural candidates forget protected static ports
nodes.invalidation: Reject the capacity claim if prompt rotation ceases to worsen matched RGB, generation uses a source image, private generator, trainable Pythia, frozen-decoder sampling, or a second visual backbone. Do not promote the candidate until natural T2I and every protected static gate pass in one independently reloaded checkpoint.

nodes.title: Rehearsal-controlled token admission protocol
nodes.motivation: Separate readout capacity from training-protocol causes before conceding that the terminal Slice reader cannot drive a frozen causal LM.
nodes.action: Full-bank diagnostic of the published candidate with per-cell records and gate-value tracking, then a preregistered ladder: E1 pure-I2T 2000 steps at lr 3e-4 with hard-cell replay; E1b identical but with the visual residual gate started at embedding magnitude (initial_proj_trust 0.2); E3 penultimate-layer H-only experts (rejected by X-invariance test before training); E2 joint training from E1 with i2t_heavy cycle, hard replay, and Adam-state resume; E2b finishing at lr 3e-5 with answer-set contrast coefficient 10.
nodes.conclusion: The published 0.444 I2T was protocol-limited. E1 raises the isolated ceiling to 0.667/0.689 with the gate pinned near zero, so step count, not gate amplitude, was binding; E1b lands worse (0.556), refuting the amplitude hypothesis and showing the optimizer holds a small visual gate as a local optimum. E2 disproves rehearsal interference as inevitable: I2T rises to 0.778 while T2T/IT2T return to 1.000 within 400 steps. E2b crosses the 0.80 admission floor at step 100 (0.822/0.811) with all static gates intact. The wrong-cell gap structure (mean gap 1.27 on wrong cells versus 4.29 on right cells at E0) already indicated readout signal-to-noise, not missing causality, was the constraint.
issues: Admission state is a single eval point of a finishing run; neighbor evals oscillate 0.73-0.79
The audited bank overlaps the training bank by construction
One seed and one synthetic scene family
The winning lever is a training protocol, so its interaction with future open-domain data is untested
nodes.invalidation: Revise the protocol conclusion if a second seed fails to reproduce admission, if removing hard replay or the i2t_heavy cycle from the same chain still admits, or if the admitted checkpoint fails its read-only re-verification.

nodes.title: Protocol ladder on natural T2I write capacity
nodes.motivation: N099 rejected natural content capacity from a 600-step diagnostic, but the token line had just shown that apparent ceilings in this stack can be step-count artifacts; the structural-versus-protocol question needed the same E-series ladder before any write-path redesign.
nodes.action: Rerun the registered N099 capacity diagnostic (two fixed ShareGPT-4o targets, 64x64, 64 slices, generation_capacity phase, gaussian-variance shortcut off, edge loss strengthened) with 25x the steps in three stages: 6000 steps at lr 3e-4/2e-4, 6000 continuation steps at half rate, and 3000 finishing steps at one-twentieth rate. Score with the unchanged natural content gate (PSNR >= 20 dB, prompt retrieval, edge relative MSE <= 0.75, edge correlation >= 0.50) on the independently reloaded candidate.
nodes.conclusion: The gate still fails, but the failure mode is revised. Edge correlation rises 0.194 to 0.351 to 0.422 to 0.448 and PSNR 15.6 to 22.1 dB; the gallery shows correct low-frequency layout, object placement, backlight gradient, and an emerging mask eye-opening. The last stage gained only +0.026 edge correlation, so the overfit asymptote of the current write path sits near 0.46-0.48, below the 0.50 gate. Protocol repair contributes 2.3x edge fidelity but cannot close the content gate: the Slice/Deslice write has a genuine high-frequency expressivity limit, distinct from N099's total-failure reading and from the read-side protocol win.
issues: Two targets, one seed, one resolution
The 0.50 edge gate itself is a registered heuristic, not a perceptual floor
Static ports are intentionally destroyed by the capacity phase (digit 0.085), so no candidate exists to promote
Write-assignment sharpening has not been tried; the asymptote could still move under a mechanism change
nodes.invalidation: Upgrade to a protocol-only failure if a registered write-side mechanism change is unnecessary, that is, if further honest budget or replay variants alone push edge correlation through 0.50; downgrade to a hard structural rejection if a matched write-sharpened variant shows no asymptote change.
